newsitem.title: USA: Ohio school vouchers overturned by appeals court.
newsitem.headline: Ohio school vouchers overturned by appeals court.

text.p: An Ohio appeals court panel struck down a school voucher pilot program in Cleveland that permits low-income residents to send their children to private schools.

The panel ruled Thursday that the program violated the Ohio constitution's establishment clause requiring separation of church and state, overturning a lower court judge who had upheld the use of vouchers.
State officials will ask the appeals court next week to stay the ruling while they ask the Ohio Supreme Court to review it, Deputy Attorney General Mark Weaver said Friday.
The decision will not force a change in the current school year, but it could affect the program next year, Weaver said.
Ohio Gov. George Voinovich and legislators established the experiment to give 1,800 Cleveland children the option of attending private or parochial schools.

The program uses a lottery to decide which students can receive vouchers worth either $2,250 or the actual tuition, whichever is less. Voinovich plans to expand the program to include 3,100 students in the next fiscal biennium beginning July 1.
"We hope to put this on hold until the appeals process is completed," Weaver said.
